newsitem.title: UK: UK MINISTER SAYS LONG-TERM JOBLESS YOUTH A PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: UK MINISTER SAYS LONG-TERM JOBLESS YOUTH A PROBLEM.

text.p: British Education and Employment Minister Baroness Blackstone said on Wednesday a fall in overall joblessness was welcome but long-term youth unemployment remained a problem.
The minister, in a statement released after British labour data were published, also said average earnings figures were "particularly encouraging."
"This is another welcome drop in the jobless total, particularly the indicators that more school and college leavers are finding work," Blackstone said.
"However, long-term youth unemployment remains a problem. One in five people unemployed for six months or more is under 25."
Blackstone said a labour force survey for the spring had showed employment was rising 20,000 to 40,000 and unemployment falling by 20,000 to 35,000 per month.
"Today's figures indicate that this improvement has continued into the summer with further falls in claimant unemployment and new vacancies continuing to be notified at a high level."
Blackstone added: "It is particularly encouraging that earnings growth remains broadly stable."
